data.why: The repo bundles real EuroSAT sample images under data/processed for upload testing, but data/multitemporal (the Cerrado imagery) and outputs/model_cerrado_resnet18.pth are both .gitignore'd and absent from the repo, so a seed script generates synthetic multitemporal pairs and a randomly-initialized ResNet18 checkpoint during install so the app can start and the comparison workflow is exercisable.

goals: Compare pre- and post-period satellite imagery of a region to screen for vegetation loss (deforestation) or gain (regeneration)
Quantify the percentage and area (hectares, given a pixel resolution) of vegetation gain, loss, and stable cover between two dates
Visually inspect HSV- and ExG-derived vegetation masks and tune thresholds to assess their sensitivity on a given scene
Screen a trained classifier's vegetation-vs-deforestation call on an individual scene
Manually label scenes as vegetation or deforestation to build a reference dataset
Save a difference heatmap and quantitative summary for a chosen area and year pair

review.summary: The tree captures the dashboard's purpose well: single-scene HSV/ExG masks, a placeholder classifier call, and a two-date gain/loss heatmap with pixel, percent and hectare totals. All ten screens I checked match their nodes, and it honestly records the state-desync bug and that the comparison ignores the ExG switch. It needs small fixes before filing: it wrongly says the repo has no labelling interface (app/rotulador.py exists but was never started), it lacks a classifier-readout feature, and it should fold the Fullscreen task into t6 and tone down 'how sure' and 'more accurate'.
